items.stem: Why does a bulb light only when the circuit is complete?

options.text: Electric current can flow all the way around the loop
options.rationale: Correct: current needs a complete, unbroken loop to flow and light the bulb.

options.text: The bulb stores its own electricity
options.rationale: The bulb needs current from the battery through a complete circuit.

options.text: Light is made by the plastic case
options.rationale: The glowing part needs current flowing through it.

options.text: Only one wire is ever needed
options.rationale: A complete loop needs the current path to return to the battery.

items.explanation: Correct: current needs a complete, unbroken loop to flow and light the bulb.

items.stem: Which TWO materials are good electrical conductors? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: copper metal conducts electricity well.
Correct: steel is a metal and conducts electricity.
Rubber is an insulator and does not conduct.
Plastic is an insulator and does not conduct.

items.explanation: Correct: copper metal conducts electricity well.

items.stem: Two magnets push away from each other when you bring them close. Why?

options.text: Two like poles are facing each other
options.rationale: Correct: like poles (N-N or S-S) repel each other.

options.text: The magnets are out of battery

options.rationale: Unlike poles attract; it is like poles that repel.
Magnets can also repel when like poles meet.

items.explanation: Correct: like poles (N-N or S-S) repel each other.
